title: Singapore launches AI agent testing kit, accredits independent testers
source_used: CNA (full text of the same article as C12-11). The MLex page (pool source) is paywalled and shows only 424 characters of boilerplate.
key_facts: IMDA launched the first version of a starter kit for testing agentic AI systems for safety and reliability on 14 Oct 2026.
AI agents, unlike conventional generative AI, can act on a user's behalf, use tools, access external systems and sensitive information and change their environment.
The kit sets out a four-step process: identify risks such as erroneous or unauthorised actions, design realistic tests, analyse logs, and continuously monitor and re-test.
It calls for testing an agent's entire trajectory, including reasoning and actions, not only its final output.
It draws on consultations with more than 20 industry deployers and testers and is a "living document" to be updated.
The AI Verify Foundation named the first five firms accredited under its AI Tester Accreditation Programme (AI TAP): AIDX Tech, Knovel Engineering, PwC Singapore, Resaro and Vulcan.
Accreditation lasts one year, and IMDA chief executive Ng Cher Pong said it does not suggest one firm can test everything.
quote_evidence: IMDA also launched the first version of a starter kit aimed at helping organisations test agentic AI systems for safety and reliability.
It also calls for testing an agent’s entire trajectory, including its reasoning and actions, rather than looking only at its final output.
They are: AIDX Tech, Knovel Engineering, PwC Singapore, Resaro and Vulcan.
why_it_matters_hint: Singapore gives companies a recognised way to test AI agents and a list of approved outside testers.
notes: MLex original is paywalled; the facts come from the CNA article, which is also the source of C12-11 (task force). Consider merging the two if the editors see them as one story.
